art.prompt: E · Read about the art here
art.done: You have done the whole art walk along the blue line. The world’s longest art exhibition, they say.

Kungsträdgården: The artist Ulrik Samuelson made the station in 1977 as an excavated garden, with finds from the Makalös palace that once stood above it. In the game: the green vault, the red and white check and the fluted columns.
T-Centralen: In 1975 Per Olof Ultvedt painted the rock white with blue vines and leaves. Among the plants you glimpse silhouettes of the workers who blasted out the station. In the game the vines are drawn anew, in the same spirit.
Rådhuset: Here the rock looks like an excavation in terracotta, with fragments sticking out of the walls, as if the city beneath the city had been dug up. The game’s version is a warm cave with blocks of stone around the tunnel mouths.
Fridhemsplan: The game’s take: muted shores, stones in display cases and a wooden bird hanging over the platform. The blue line’s stations are blasted caves, and here the rock gets to be a beach.
Stadshagen: Stadshagen lies near the sports grounds on Kungsholmen. The game gives the station a red running track that follows the wall all the way round.
Västra skogen: The western forest: the game draws white birch trunks on dark green rock. Here the line splits, toward Akalla one way and Hjulsta the other.
Solna centrum: Karl-Olov Björk and Anders Åberg painted a burning red evening sky over a dark spruce forest, with pictures of how the forest and the countryside are changing. It is one of the metro’s best-known stations.
Näckrosen: The game’s take on the name, which means water lily: pale water with floating lily pads. In reality the station has motifs from the film studios in Råsunda next door.
Hallonbergen: The art here is built on children’s drawings: cheerful figures and scribbles in crayon colours on white. The game makes its own squiggles.
Kista: Kista is the town of computers and phones. The game’s take: dark blue rock with bright traces, like a circuit board.
Husby: The game’s take: ochre rock and blue flowers low on the walls, like a meadow on Järvafältet.
Akalla: Akalla is known for its large painted tiles with scenes from everyday life. The game puts tile panels in yellow, blue and red at eye level.
Huvudsta: The game’s take: grey-blue rock with a narrow band of gold high up on the wall.
Solna strand: The game’s take: a pale sky with drifting clouds, so the rock feels lighter.
Sundbybergs centrum: The game’s take: warm yellow rock and brick-red stripes at the bottom. Here you change to the commuter trains and Tvärbanan.
Duvbo: The game’s take: deep blue-green water with bubbles rising toward the vault.
Rissne: Rissne has a timeline through history along its walls. The game draws a dark band with year markings that runs the whole length of the platform.
Rinkeby: The game’s take: glints of gold in dark rock, like finds from the earth.
Tensta: The game’s take: a colourful mural where many colours and people meet.
Hjulsta: The end of the line. The game draws orange wheels on dark rock, since hjul means wheel.

clipping: Yellowed, from 1981: ”Spöktåget: föraren som vägrar köra efter midnatt. ’Hon kommer utan ljud. Står det Kymlinge på skylten ska man inte kliva på’, säger en förare som vill vara anonym.”
logbook: A driver’s handwritten logbook. The last spread: ”03.47. Silverfärgat tåg på spår 1, ej i tidtabellen. Inga ljus i hytten. Följde efter till vändspåret. Där fanns inget spår.” Someone has torn out the next page.
scratches: Someone has scratched into the concrete with a key: ”HON STANNAR FÖR DEM SOM VÄNTAR. STANNA INTE KVAR EFTER KYMLINGE.”
clock: The clock at Kymlinge stands at 03.47, the same minute as in the logbook.
lastPage: The page torn out of the logbook: ”Jag stannade kvar ombord förbi Kymlinge. Jag vaknade på en bänk på Kungsträdgården klockan fem, när första tåget gick. Det var samma morgon igen.”

loop.wake: You wake up on a bench at Kungsträdgården. It is just before five in the morning and the first train is about to leave. It is the same morning again.
loop.back: You blink. The clock is right again.
